statement: Let A and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let F:A→B be an additive functor preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Give each finite-filtered bounded-below localization its cone-normalized triangulation, and let S and T be any representative-normalized truncation calculi on these localizations [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus-base]. Then there exist a functor L:DF⁺(A)→DF⁺(B), natural isomorphisms eω:L⋙T.ω≅S.ω⋙D(F), egr(r):L⋙T.gr(r)≅S.gr(r)⋙D(F), and eh:S.high(0)⋙S.ω⋙D(F)≅L⋙T.high(0)⋙T.ω such that, for every X, eh_X followed by T.ω of the high-zero inclusion at LX and then eω_X equals D(F) applied to S.ω of the inclusion at X; and eh_X followed by the normalized grade-zero projection at LX and then egr(0)_X equals D(F) of the normalized grade-zero projection at X. Here D(F) is the ordinary derived functor of the exact functor F, high is filtration subcomplex truncation, and grade-zero projection is from ω high(0) to gr(0), with the actual inclusion and quotient maps on representatives. Filtrations are uniformly finite, independently of the cochain bound, as in [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients].

proof.text: Apply F termwise to the underlying complex. Define the pth new filtration step as the image of F of the original step inclusion. The mapped original step is monic, hence its factorization onto that image is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms are natural and commute with step inclusions. The original top/bottom filtration indices and lower cochain bound remain valid, including zero complexes and empty filtration support.

F preserves cokernels. Comparing the cokernel of consecutive mapped step inclusions with the new filtration quotient gives a natural graded-complex isomorphism. Its quotient square commutes by the cokernel universal property. Therefore graded quasi-isomorphisms remain graded quasi-isomorphisms. Descend the filtered coefficient functor and its underlying and graded comparisons using the localization universal property and the ordinary exact derived functor comparison.

The high-truncation inclusion is injective on Hom from an object supported in filtration indices at least r, by the high Hom bijection of the universal truncation triangle. Its support and representative normalization apply to actual high complexes. This proves naturality of the normalized high comparison of any truncation calculus, by composing the desired equation with the inclusion and cancelling. The mapped step isomorphisms therefore give the high-zero underlying comparison.

On representatives, expand the three descended comparisons. Naturality cancels the localization comparison isomorphisms. The inclusion equation reduces to the image factorization of the mapped step inclusion. The projection equation reduces to the cokernel quotient square from step 2. The prescribed normalizations of S and T identify these equations with the requested maps. Whiskering with the localization functor is faithful on natural transformations, so the equations hold on all localized objects.
